t: You're in Kensington Gardens, which were once part of the private gardens of Kensington Palace and are now one of the Royal Parks, largely open to the public. They cover 107 hectares, sit just west of Hyde Park, and are shared by Westminster and the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea. Together with Hyde Park, Green Park and St. James's Park they form a green lung in the heart of London. The entomologist Theresa Clay lived here. She became the world's expert on chewing lice.
